Sheshegwaning First Nation

Sheshegwaning First Nation’s starting path follows community decision-making and educational planning. A 2024 report records citizens’ discussion of a governance agreement, while a school-design account describes collaboration on a building intended to serve Sheshegwaning and neighbouring Zhiibaahaasing children.

01

Community participation in governance

Kirk Titmuss’s April 2024 report describes Sheshegwaning citizens celebrating approval of the Anishinabek Nation Governance Agreement. Speakers including Deputy Chief Ann Cada and Elder Joseph Laford emphasized participation and decisions on community terms. The account explains a dispute over approval procedures. It records perspectives at that event; the agreement and subsequent implementation need separate review.

Read the sources [1] Anishinabek News

02

Designing a place for learning

The school’s architects describe walks, workshops and engagement with Sheshegwaning members as part of their design process. Their account connects learning spaces with the land and proposes uses beyond classroom hours, including service to children from neighbouring Zhiibaahaasing. The page mixes future and completed language, so this guide does not establish when the school opened or evaluate its results.

Read the sources [2] Architects Tillmann Ruth Robinson
